record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: How do the double-trace interfaces described holographically fuse with one another, and can that fusion process be analyzed systematically using the mixed-boundary-value and harmonic-analysis tools proposed in the paper?

evidence.quote: our aim for the near future is to investigate the fusion process of the presented double trace interfaces by these methods.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a holographic setup in which two conformal field theories CFT_+ and CFT_- are related by deformation by a double-trace scalar operator, and are joined along a codimension-one conformal interface (a "double-trace interface") realized in the bulk by imposing mixed Dirichlet–Neumann boundary conditions for a scalar field on the two sides of an asymptotically AdS geometry. Such interfaces can be analyzed by (i) solving the resulting mixed boundary-value problem for the scalar bulk-to-boundary propagator, and (ii) applying harmonic analysis on warped-product bulk geometries (so that the wave equation separates) to compute interface two-point functions and the operator spectrum localized on the interface.

Two parallel codimension-one interfaces of this type can be brought together and "fused" into a single effective interface. Develop a systematic framework, using the mixed boundary-value-problem and harmonic-analysis tools above, to describe the fusion of two such double-trace interfaces. Specifically:

1. Define the fusion of two parallel double-trace interfaces I_{a} and I_{b} (associated with double-trace deformation parameters a and b respectively) as the limit in which their separation tends to zero, and characterize the resulting interface I_{a*b} via its bulk boundary conditions and its action on bulk propagators and on the spectrum of interface operators.
2. Derive a closed-form fusion rule expressing the parameter (or boundary condition data) of I_{a*b} in terms of those of I_a and I_b, and verify associativity of the resulting fusion product.
3. Determine how the interface two-point functions and the spectrum of operators living on the fused interface are obtained from those of the constituent interfaces through the harmonic-analysis decomposition.
artifact.status_search_result: A search shows continued activity on double-trace interfaces and mixed boundary conditions in AdS/CFT (e.g., the originating "Double Trace Interfaces" work and later developments on mixed boundary conditions and double-trace-like deformations in celestial/wedge holography), but no source explicitly presents a complete, systematic fusion analysis of double-trace interfaces using the proposed mixed boundary-value and harmonic-analysis methods. The status of the specific fusion program therefore appears unresolved based on the available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Double Trace Interfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Renormalization group interfaces between two holographic CFTs related by a double-trace scalar deformation; derives interface two-point functions and operator spectra.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the holographic double-trace interface construction whose fusion the question asks about, but does not analyze fusion of two such interfaces.

status_evidence.title: Mixed boundary conditions and Double-trace like deformations in Celestial holography and Wedge-like holography
status_evidence.snippet: Studies mixed boundary conditions and double-trace-like deformations in celestial/wedge holography.
status_evidence.claim: Recent follow-up work on mixed-boundary/double-trace techniques but does not address systematic fusion of double-trace interfaces.
